_metadata.description: Must-ship requirements. Each mirrors one P0 operational target one-to-one and carries at least two automated validation layers.

requirements.description: The scenario shall create, describe, list and destroy an instance through one provider interface, and no caller shall name a provider
requirements.title: Provider-agnostic instance lifecycle

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/provider/provider_test.go [REQ tag required]. The fake provider satisfies Create, Describe, List and Destroy, and a request for a size the provider does not offer is refused before any call is made.
Intended: api/internal/instance/lifecycle_integration_test.go [REQ tag required]. A full request-to-destroyed cycle runs against the fake provider and every state transition is persisted in order.

Intended: api/internal/provider/interface_surface_test.go [REQ tag required]. An AST assertion that the Provider interface declares exactly four methods, and that no caller package imports a concrete provider implementation.

requirements.description: When an instance is requested, the scenario shall persist the request and its idempotency key before it calls any provider API
requirements.title: Intent recorded before the provider is called

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/intent/intent_test.go [REQ tag required]. An intent row carrying its idempotency key is committed before the provider client is reachable; replaying the same key returns the original intent rather than creating a second.

Intended: api/internal/intent/lost_response_integration_test.go [REQ tag required]. A provider call that succeeds while its response is lost leaves a recoverable intent that the reconciler can match to the created instance.

requirements.description: The scenario shall compare provider inventory against its own records in both directions on a schedule, and shall report every divergence rather than resolve it silently
requirements.title: Bidirectional reconciliation

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/reconcile/reconcile_test.go [REQ tag required]. Present at the provider and absent locally is reported as an orphan; present locally and absent at the provider closes the usage window instead of continuing to meter.

Intended: api/internal/reconcile/sweep_integration_test.go [REQ tag required]. A full sweep against the fake provider emits findings in both directions and mutates no instance, proving the reconciler reports rather than resolves.
An operator can quarantine a reported orphan, inspect it, and then destroy it.

requirements.description: Every instance shall carry an expiry enforced both by the scenario and by a timer on the instance itself, so the fleet drains when the scenario is unavailable
requirements.title: Expiry enforced twice

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/expiry/sweeper_test.go [REQ tag required]. The sweeper destroys instances past expiry, honours an extension granted before expiry, and refuses to extend one already destroyed.

Intended: api/internal/expiry/firstboot_timer_test.go [REQ tag required]. The rendered first-boot configuration contains a timer that powers the instance off at its expiry without contacting the control plane.
With this scenario stopped, an instance past its expiry still powers itself off.

requirements.description: When an instance boots it shall become a trusted node through the bridge onboarding contract, with no interactive step and no password on any wire
requirements.title: Unattended enrollment

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/enroll/firstboot_test.go [REQ tag required]. The rendered first-boot configuration carries the bridge onboarding public key and no password, token or private key of any kind.

Intended: api/internal/enroll/bridge_integration_test.go [REQ tag required]. Against a bridge fake, the scenario creates the machine record with its locators and starts onboarding; no credential value appears in any request field or log line.
A real provisioned instance reaches the online state with no interactive step performed by the operator.

requirements.description: When provisioned compute is requested, the scenario shall reserve credit server-side before it calls a provider, and shall settle measured usage when the instance is destroyed
requirements.title: Credit reserved before boot

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/meter/reserve_test.go [REQ tag required]. A reservation is obtained before the provider client is reachable, and a refused reservation short-circuits with no provider call and a distinguishable out-of-credit outcome.

Intended: api/internal/meter/settle_integration_test.go [REQ tag required]. Teardown settles measured usage against the reservation, and a provision that fails after reserving releases the reservation rather than burning it.

Intended: api/internal/meter/enforcement_boundary_test.go [REQ tag required]. A client asserting a higher tier than its subscription is still refused, because the tier is resolved server-side and never read from the request.

requirements.description: The scenario shall expose no pause that maps to a provider power-off, because a stopped instance still bills at the full rate on most providers
requirements.title: Destroy is the only stop

validation.notes: Intended: api/internal/provider/no_pause_test.go [REQ tag required]. An AST assertion that no exported method, handler or domain function named pause, stop, suspend, halt or shutdown exists anywhere in the scenario.
Intended: cli/domains/instance/verbs_test.go [REQ tag required]. The CLI manifest declares no pause, stop or suspend verb, and the destroy verb is the only lifecycle terminator.
